claims.text: DCI Allen W. Dulles wrote to him on 18 January 1958 as 'Chief of Research and Development, Department of the Army': 'Congratulations on your appointment as Chief of the Army Research and Development program.'

He signed his letter of 24 February 1962 to DCI John A. McCone as 'ARTHUR G. TRUDEAU / Lieutenant General, GS / Chief of Research and Development', inviting the Director to a symposium on 'The U. S. Army's Limited-War Mission and Social Science Research' hosted by the Special Operations Research Office of The American University on 26 to 28 March 1962.

McCone's reply of 12 March 1962, reference ER 62-1185/a, is addressed 'Lieut. General Arthur G. Trudeau, Chief of Research and Development, Department of the Army' and declines, designating a representative whose name is withheld from the release.

claims.text: The 'Gen. Arthur S. Trudeau' named in the 1955 FBI material quoted in philip-corso.narrative is most probably this officer. Reasoning: the two primary letters opened here give the middle initial G over his own signature, and no second Army general officer of that surname was found. The discrepancy is unresolved and no record opened here reconciles it.

label: Lt. Gen. Arthur G. Trudeau
narrative: Arthur G. Trudeau held the Army post that sat directly above the office Philip Corso's service record places him in. Two CIA records fix it. Allen Dulles congratulated him on the appointment in January 1958, and in February 1962 Trudeau wrote to Director of Central Intelligence John McCone over his own signature as Lieutenant General, GS, Chief of Research and Development. Corso's DA Form 66 records him as Chief of the Foreign Technology Division, OCRD, from 18 April to 18 July 1962, which falls inside Trudeau's tenure. That is the whole of the documented relationship. No independent record of a Foreign Technology Division inside OCRD was opened, so this node is Trudeau and the office, not the division. The distribution-conduit account attached to Corso is not evidence about Trudeau, and nothing opened for this pass connects him to it.
